chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is not permissible for two women to spend the night in one quilt, unless there is a partition between them. If they do so, they are prohibited from that. If they are found after the prohibition, each one of them is whipped a hadd (a fixed penalty). If they are found again in one quilt, they are whipped. If they are found for the third time, they are killed.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal penalty for two women sharing a bed without a partition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the progressive penal stages for female same-sex intercourse (liwat al-nisa), moving from prohibition to flogging and ultimately execution upon a third recurrence. It reflects the Shia juristic tradition of applying the hadd penalty for liwat to women, mirroring the severity accorded to men, while emphasizing the evidentiary requirement of repeated acts to escalate the punishment.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Raham Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It is not for the two women that they should be sleeping in one quilt, except that there happens to be in between the two of them, a partition. So if they were to do that, they should be prevented from that. So if they were to be found after having been prevented, each one of them would be whipped a Penalty (Hadd), a Penalty (Hadd) (one hundred lashes each). So if they were both found again in one quilt, they would be whipped. So if they were found for the third times, they would both be killed’.
